text:
elena-cs: Hey folks — I’m drafting the customer follow-up for the outage last night (hosted API). Wanted to drop a draft and get quick sign-off from SRE/Eng/Legal. Posting proposed status & customer email below, pls comment inline.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0421 detected. Severity: P2 -> P1 escalation. Affected service: hosted inference (text-generation v2 route). Alerts started at ~2026-04-21 22:08 UTC, mitigation began 22:40 UTC, service recovered 23:05 UTC.

tom-oncall: quick timeline from my side: 22:08 first alert (error spike + latency), 22:12 paging, 22:20 discovered high error rate tied to a config rollout that changed KV-cache TTLs for a subset of hosts, 22:40 we rolled back the rollout which reduced 5xxs, 22:58 stabilization checks passed, 23:05 full traffic back. Root cause: a config/rollout that shortened KV cache TTLs combined with a routing change caused cache churn and overloaded inference workers.

maria-product: Customer impact note: ~18% peak 5xx rate across the cluster; approx 30 customers saw degraded responses or elevated latency; largest impacted customer: ACME Corp (about 5% of traffic through the affected route). No data exfiltration.

elena-cs: DRAFT status page blurb (please keep short + non-technical):
```
We experienced degraded API availability for the hosted inference service on 2026-04-21 from 22:08 to 23:05 UTC. Some requests returned errors or experienced increased latency. We identified a configuration rollout as the cause and reverted the change; service has been restored and is being monitored. A follow-up with further details and mitigation actions will be provided within 72 hours.
```

ben-ops: Keep it exactly like that but do not mention internal component names (KV cache) — say "configuration rollout" only. Also add a line about credits if Finance ok.

carla-eng: Also add one short line confirming no customer data was accessed: "No customer data was exposed." I'll add monitoring links and a postmortem link once it's published.

tom-oncall: Verified metrics: peak error rate 18.2% at ~22:22 UTC, total error volume ~1.1M requests across the cluster during the window, affected tokens estimate ~6.4M. Those numbers can be included in internal RCA but don't put into customer-facing note.

elena-cs: DRAFT customer email for ACME (sensitive customer) — feedback welcome.
```
Hi <Customer Contact>,

We wanted to let you know about an incident that affected Redwood's hosted inference service on 2026-04-21 between 22:08 and 23:05 UTC. During this window, some API requests to text-generation routes experienced increased latency and occasional errors.

What happened: We deployed a configuration change that unintentionally reduced cache stability for a subset of hosts, which increased load on inference workers and caused elevated error rates. We reverted the change, and the service is now restored.

Impact: Some requests may have returned errors or been slower than usual. We saw a peak error rate of ~18% for a short interval. We do not believe any customer data was exposed.

What we’re doing: Our engineering team has rolled back the change, applied a mitigation to prevent immediate recurrence, and is performing a full RCA. We will share a post-incident report with key findings and long-term fixes within 72 hours.

If you saw any specific failed requests you want us to review, please reply with the request IDs or timestamps and we’ll prioritize those.

We apologize for the disruption and appreciate your patience.

— Elena, Customer Success (on behalf of Redwood Inference)
```

maria-product: Suggest adding: "As a gesture of goodwill, we will apply a service credit for the impacted time window" (Finance sign-off pending).

ben-ops: Legal/Compliance ok with the wording and the 72h promise. Keep the "no customer data exposed" line.

carla-eng: Postmortem plan: Tom + Eng will produce a full RCA doc with timeline, root cause, corrective actions, and code/config changes. I'll attach it to the customer email when available. Proposed immediate prevents: 1) add rollout guardrail to verify cache TTLs before rollout, 2) add alerting for cache-churn patterns, 3) limit rollout concurrency for config pushes.

tom-oncall: I'll own the RCA. Next steps and owners:
- Tom: deep-dive and publish RCA (ETA 72hrs)
- Carla: implement rollout guardrail & alert (ETA 7 days)
- Eng-oncall: run 48-hr canary for config changes on low-traffic pools (ETA immediate)

elena-cs: Action items for customer comms (I will own send):
- Finalize and send ACME email at 10:00 UTC tomorrow (need final numbers from Tom)
- Post status page update now with blurb above (guarded wording)
- Follow-up with full RCA link when available (within 72 hours)

tom-oncall: I'll DM you final verified numbers in ~30m. Also adding an internal note: we should add a short "what we changed" summary in the RCA showing the exact config key + rollout ID (internal only).

elena-cs: Thanks everyone — please react with :thumbsup: when you sign off on the customer email. I'll wait for Tom's numbers before sending.

carla-eng: :thumbsup: signed.

ben-ops: :thumbsup:

maria-product: :thumbsup: 

incident-bot: Reminder: Post-incident RCA required within 72h. Assigning incident INC-2026-0421 to Tom for RCA publication.

elena-cs: Closing note — if anyone hears from customers directly before we send, ping me immediately so we can coordinate responses. Thanks.
